For State : Mr. Ruhul Ameen Memon, P. L.
 Hon'ble Smt. Justice Rajani Dubey  C.A.V. ORDER 1.

The petitioner has filed the instant writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for issuance of appropriate writ of mandamus and certiorari and for other suitable writs and directions against the order dated 30.03.2017 passed by the respondent Director General of Police, Raipur by which it has been stated inter alia that in Departmental proceeding, the petitioner has been held guilty.
The criminal action and departmental action are two different things, as in both the charges are different.
2. Brief facts of the case as adumbrated by the petitioner is that the petitioner was posted on the post of Constable R-340 in Rakshit Kendra Janjgir-Champa, District Janjgir-Champa (C.G.).
On 11.02.2010, one Dharmendra Dewangan has given information to the Police Station that one female Constable Sarita Singh who resides as a tenant in his house has hanged herself.
The Police Station Champa has registered morgue vide No. 13/10.
The suicide note of the deceased has been seized.
In morgue enquiry, it was found that there was a love affair between constable Sarita Singh and the petitioner.

Though the petitioner has made a commitment to marry the deceased, on the other hand,
he planned to do marriage with someone else.
When deceased Sarita Singh asked regarding the same to the petitioner, he then gave her reply that if you want to die, then go and die.
On that pretext, Sarita Singh committed suicide on 11.02.2010.
Thereafter, the charge-sheet has been filed vide No. 145/10 dated 29.06.2010.

Sessions Trial No. 108/2010 has been registered at Sessions Judge Janjgir-Champa, State of Chhattisgarh through "Rakshit Kendra" Champa, District Janjgir-Champa v. Syed Khurshid Ali for an offence under Section 306 of IPC.

sentences.text: Against this order dated 16.02.2012, the petitioner preferred an appeal before the respondent Inspector General of Police, Bilaspur but the office of Inspector General of Police in a note sheet has stated that as the appeal is pending in High Court of Chhattisgarh against the order dated 04.04.2011, till the decision of appeal by the High Court of Chhattisgarh, the matter be kept pending amounting order of High Court of Chhattisgarh.

The State of Chhattisgarh filed an appeal before this Court which was registered as Acquittal Appeal No. 72/2012 and vide order dated 12.07.2016, the Court has dismissed the Acquittal Appeal, but the appellate authority, Inspector General of Police has passed the impugned order Annexure P-2 dated 15.11.2016, whereby the appeal of the petitioner was dismissed.

The petitioner has preferred an appeal before the DGP in which inter alia it has been mentioned that Inspector General of Police has kept in abeyance by mentioning the reason that the matter is subjudice before the High Court of Chhattisgarh and once the High Court of Chhattisgarh and once the High Court of Chhattisgarh has dismissed the acquittal appeal of the State, the Inspector General of Police should have followed the same.

The DGP has heard the mercy petition of the petitioner and has given the finding that the Hon'ble High Court vide order dated 12.07.2016 upheld the order passed by the Session Judge in which the petitioner has been exonerated under Section 306 of IPC.
As in the Departmental proceeding, the petitioner has been held guilty as the criminal judicial action and departmental action are two different things, as in both the charges are different.
Therefore, the DGP also dismissed the mercy petition vide order dated 31.03.2017 (Annexure P/01).

The petitioner also moved mercy petition before respondent No. 1, but vide order dated 27.05.2017, it has been informed to the petitioner that there is no provision to appeal before the State as per para 262 of Police Regulation Act, 1861.

The action of respondent/State is pick and choose, as in some cases where the employee of constable has been exonerated in criminal case, the Departmental Enquiry has not been done and the employee/constable has been reinstated.

In the case of Surendra Khandekar when he has been exonerated from the criminal case he is taken back in the service vider order dated 03.10.2015 passed by the Superintendent of Police Janjgir- Champa.
The respondent authority did not consider the Police Regulation No. 241 and passed impugned orders against the petitioner which are liable to be set aside.
So, the impugned orders dated 31.03.2017 (Annexure P/01), 15.11.2016 (Annexure P/02) & 16.02.2012 (Annexure P/03) are liable to be set aside.

sentences.text:
Ex adverso, learned counsel for the respondents No. 1 to 4 strongly oppose the prayer of the petitioner and submits that the petitioner was posted at Police Station Champa and during that time, love affair was developed between the petitioner and one lady Constable Sarita Singh who was also posted at Police Station Champa, and on giving false allurement of marriage and when the petitioner denied for marriage, she committed suicide and on account of the same, an offence under Section 306 of IPC was registered against the petitioner and after completion of usual investigation,
a final charge-sheet was filed before the learned trial Court and after completion of trial, the petitioner was acquitted of the charges.

After registration of offence, a preliminary inquiry was conducted against the petitioner in which the petitioner was found guilty while holding the post of Constable, the petitioner has violated the provisions of the Police Regulation and accordingly a Departmental Enquiry was instituted against the petitioner by issuing the charge-sheet Annexure P/05 and petitioner duly replied the said charge-sheet vide Annexure R/01.

The petitioner duly participated in the Departmental Enquiry, which was initiated by the Enquiry Officer and the petitioner was duly afforded due opportunity for defending his case in the departmental enquiry instituted against him.

The inquiry officer field report vide Annexure R/02 and as per this report,
the Inquiry Officer has found the charges leveled against the petitioner proved.

From bare perusal of the Enquiry report it would be evident that the Departmental Enquiry has been conducted strictly in accordance with law by providing full opportunity of hearing to the petitioner.

After receipt of the enquiry report from the Inquiry Officer, the disciplinary authority i.e., the Superintendent of Police has issued notice dated 05.11.2011 to the petitioner, seeking explanation on the enquiry report dated and the petitioner has duly submitted the reply (Annexure R-03).
Upon the reply being found dissatisfactory, the Disciplinary Authority has passed order of removal from service dated 16.02.2012 (Annexure P-03).

The petitioner filed appeal against this order and the appellate authority has considered all grounds of appeal and has dismissed the appeal vide order dated 24.10.2013 (Annexure P-01) and the petitioner has preferred an appeal against the order dated 16.02.2012 (Annexure P-03)

, the Inspector General of Police, Bilaspur has dismissed the appeal preferred by the petitioner and the order of the Disciplinary Authority has been affirmed vide order dated 15.11.2016 (Annexure P-02).
Thereafter, the petitioner has preferred a mercy appeal before the Director General of Police, Chhattisgarh which has also been rejected vide impugned order dated 31.03.2017 (Annexure P/01).

It is a well settled principle of law that the orders passed by the Administrative Authorities in the departmental enquiry proceedings can only be challenged on the ground of violation of rules applicable in the departmental enquiry proceedings and the scope of interference by the High Court is very limited that too the extent of decision making process only and not to the decision.

The petitioner has not alleged violation of any rule in initiating the departmental enquiry proceedings and, therefore, the orders passed by the administrative authority in the departmental enquiry proceedings cannot be questioned, which has been initiated strictly in accordance with law.

He further submits that the petitioner was a member of disciplined force, and while when he was in service he committed heinous offence and the same falls under the moral turpitude and, therefore, the petitioner was not found suitable and fit for the services of the Police Department as the Police Department is a disciplined force and every officer requires discipline in all manner so that a positive message can be conveyed to the society.
Therefore, the petitioner cannot take any benefit from the order (Annexure P-08) as the case of the petitioner is entirely and factually distinguishable from the case of Surendra Khandekar.
So, this petition is being devoid of any merit, and the same is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: Heard both the counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
8. It is not disputed that the petitioner was working as a Constable in Police Department.
A criminal case was registered against him under Section 306 of IPC.
The learned Session Court acquitted the petitioner and the State filed appeal against this acquittal and the acquittal appeal was also dismissed by the High Court.
It is also not disputed that for the same act, a Departmental Enquiry was initiated against the petitioner and the Disciplined Authority passed order of termination (Annexure P-03) dated 16.02.2012.

The petitioner filed appeal against this order and appellate authority dismissed his appeal on 15.11.2016 and the petitioner then filed mercy petition before the DGP, which was also dismissed by impugned order dated 31.03.2017 (Annexure P-01)
9.

Main ground of the petitioner is that the Departmental Enquiry and Criminal proceedings, both were based on identical and similar facts and, therefore, in the light of Regulation 241 of C.G. Police Regulation as a matter of right the petitioner is entitled for reinstatement and orders of all the authorities are liable to be set aside.

10. This Court held in WPS No. 83 of 2016 paragraphs 8, 9, 10, 11 & 17 which reads as under:-
"8. In order to consider the plea as to whether the petitioner is entitled for the benefit of Regulation 241 of the Chhattisgarh Police Regulations, it would be appropriate to notice Regulation 241 of the said Regulations which states as under:-
"241. Cases of acquittal When a police officer has been tried and acquitted by a criminal court, he must as a rule be to reinstated.
He may not be punished departmentally when the offence for which he was tried constitutes the sole ground of punishment.
If, however the acquittal, whether in the court of original jurisdiction or of appeal was based on technical grounds.

Or if the facts established at the trial show that his retention in Government service is undesirable, the Superintendent may take departmental cognizance of his conduct, after obtaining the sanction of the Inspector-General."

9. A careful perusal of Regulation 241 of the Chhattisgarh Police Regulations would show that it is an exception to the rule applicable to the police force providing that once an employee has been acquitted by the criminal court, as a matter of right, he should be reinstated in service and he may not be punished departmentally when the offence for which he was tried constituted the sole ground of punishment.

However, Regulation 241 also carves out a caveat that if the order of acquittal is based on technical grounds or if the facts established at the trial show that his retention in Government Service is undesirable, the Superintendent may take departmental cognizance of his conduct, after obtaining the sanction of the Inspector General.

sentences.text: The provisions contained in Regulation 241 of the Chhattisgarh Police Regulations came up for consideration before the Full Bench of the M.P. High Court in the matter of Harinarayan Ramratan Dubey.

Khandwa v. State of Madhya Pradesh and others reported in 1975 MPLJ 429 in which the scope and ambit of Regulation 241 was considered and it has been held as under:-
"The regulation thus prohibits departmental punishment for the offence of which an officer has been acquitted by a competent Court.

entities.text: Khandwa v. State of Madhya Pradesh and others reported in 1975 MPLJ 429
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It however makes an exception in the case where acquittal was based on technical grounds.
But the exception itself is made subject to a condition precedent that no departmental enquiry should be held without obtaining the sanction of the Inspector General of Police.

Another provision in the para is that when an officer has been acquitted but the facts established at the trial show that his retention in Government service is undesirable, departmental action can be taken; but there also subject to the condition precedent that the sanction of the Inspector General of Police must be obtained in the first instance."

"11. This Court also in the matter of Pohari Sharan Pandey v. State of M.P (now CG) and the Superintendent of Police reported in 2007 LawSuit (Chh) 118 has considered the scope and ambit of Regulation 241 of the Chhattisgarh Police Regulations and held as under:-
"14.

entities.text: Pohari Sharan Pandey v. State of M.P
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case in hand the charge in the criminal case as well as in the departmental enquiry was one and the same.
The alleged forged police rojnamcha sanha was produced before the Magistrate.
Shri A.H. Khan, the then Incharge was also examined and cross examined.

The Magistrate had found that the witness Shri P.R.
Sao had admitted the alleged forged bills as genuine.

Then then S.D.O.(P) Shri G.R.
Shrivastava also supported the case of the petitioner and the criminal Court found that the prosecution was lodged on account of the malice on the part of the Police Station Incharge Shri A.H. Khan towards the petitioner.
In the departmental enquiry Shri P.R. Sao and Shri A.H. Khan were also examined.
The then S.D.O. (P) was not examined, under whom the petitioner had actually worked, at the relevant time but other S.D.O. (P) Shri P. N. Awasthi was examined.

Thus, it is found that the evidence and the documents produced before the criminal Court, as well as before the enquiry authority, were almost the same, except that some new witnesses like Shri P.N.
Awasthi, S.D.O. (P), who was not S.D.O. (P) at the relevant time, were examined in the departmental enquiry.
The petitioner is entitled to the benefit under Regulation 241 of the Regulations, which is statutory in nature.

Regulation 241 clearly mandates that when a police officer has been tried and acquitted in a criminal Court, he must,
as a rule, be reinstated.
He may not be punished departmentally when the offence for which he was tried constitutes the sole ground of punishment.
In the case of acquittal on technical grounds, the departmental cognizance of misconduct may be taken after obtaining the sanction of the Inspector General of Police.
In the present case there was clear cut exoneration and there was no finding against the petitioner that he was undesirable in service.

17. Thus, from the aforesaid analysis, it is quite established that charges in the departmental proceeding were based on the allegation that the petitioner abetted the commission of suicide of his wife and treated her with cruelty which is punishable under Sections 306 & 498A of the IPC and since he is said to have not maintained good relationship with his wife ans is said to have acted violently with his wife, therefore, departmental proceeding was initiated against him in which he was punished also, departmentally.

But when the matter was remanded to consider afresh by order dated 12.02.2015, the two authorities refused to grant the benefit of Regulation 241 of the Police Regulations on the ground that the charges are not one and same in both the proceedings i.e.
criminal and departmental and both the charges are different, whereas, as noticed above, though the departmental proceeding is based on Regulation 64(11) of the Police Regulations, but the basis of invoking Regulation 64(11) is criminal behaviour i.e. the offence punishable under Sections 306 &
498A of the IPC for which he was admittedly acquitted on 28.05.1997 honourably by the criminal court and criminal appeal preferred against his acquittal has been dismissed by this Court by affirming the judgment of acquittal.

Therefore, it is clearly established that Regulation 241 of the Police Regulations is squarely attracted, as he has been tried for offence under Sections 306 & 498A of the IPC and he has been acquitted by the criminal court and his acquittal has been affirmed by this Court in criminal appeal.
Thus, as a matter of right, by Regulation 241 he is entitled to be reinstated as he cannot be punished departmentally for the offence for which he has been tried and acquitted clearly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Sessions Trial No. 108/2010 has been registered at Sessions Judge Janjgir-Champa, State of Chhattisgarh through "Rakshit Kendra" Champa, District Janjgir-Champa v. Syed Khurshid Ali for an offence under Section 306 of IPC.
The D.G.P while passing the order dated 31.03.2017 has held that as the petitioner has been acquitted of the criminal charges, but in Departmental Enquiry the charges have been proved against the petitioner and the charges of the judicial proceedings and Departmental proceedings are different, as such these are incorrect findings.
has issued the impugned order dated 16.02.2012 and terminated the services of the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is a well settled principle of law that the orders passed by the Administrative Authorities in the departmental enquiry proceedings can only be challenged on the ground of violation of rules applicable in the departmental enquiry proceedings and the scope of interference by the High Court is very limited that too the extent of decision making process only and not to the decision.
The petitioner has not alleged violation of any rule in initiating the departmental enquiry proceedings and, therefore, the orders passed by the administrative authority in the departmental enquiry proceedings cannot be questioned, which has been initiated strictly in accordance with law.
He further submits that the petitioner was a member of disciplined force, and while when he was in service he committed heinous offence and the same falls under the moral turpitude and, therefore, the petitioner was not found suitable and fit for the services of the Police Department as the Police Department is a disciplined force and every officer requires discipline in all manner so that a positive message can be conveyed to the society.
Main ground of the petitioner is that the Departmental Enquiry and Criminal proceedings, both were based on identical and similar facts and, therefore, in the light of Regulation 241 of C.G. Police Regulation as a matter of right the petitioner is entitled for reinstatement and orders of all the authorities are liable to be set aside.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
6. Reliance has been placed on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Imtiyaz Ahmad Malla Vs. State of Jammu and Kashmir and Others reported in 2023 SCC OnLine SC 205.
7.
9. A careful perusal of Regulation 241 of the Chhattisgarh Police Regulations would show that it is an exception to the rule applicable to the police force providing that once an employee has been acquitted by the criminal court, as a matter of right, he should be reinstated in service and he may not be punished departmentally when the offence for which he was tried constituted the sole ground of punishment.
However, Regulation 241 also carves out a caveat that if the order of acquittal is based on technical grounds or if the facts established at the trial show that his retention in Government Service is undesirable, the Superintendent may take departmental cognizance of his conduct, after obtaining the sanction of the Inspector General.
Syed Khurshid Ali vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196777638/
6 10.
The petitioner is entitled to the benefit under Regulation 241 of the Regulations, which is statutory in nature.
Regulation 241 clearly mandates that when a police officer has been tried and acquitted in a criminal Court, he must,
as a rule, be reinstated.
He may not be punished departmentally when the offence for which he was tried constitutes the sole ground of punishment.
In the case of acquittal on technical grounds, the departmental cognizance of misconduct may be taken after obtaining the sanction of the Inspector General of Police.
In the present case there was clear cut exoneration and there was no finding against the petitioner that he was undesirable in service.
Syed Khurshid Ali vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196777638/
7 15.
17. Thus, from the aforesaid analysis, it is quite established that charges in the departmental proceeding were based on the allegation that the petitioner abetted the commission of suicide of his wife and treated her with cruelty which is punishable under Sections 306 & 498A of the IPC and since he is said to have not maintained good relationship with his wife ans is said to have acted violently with his wife, therefore, departmental proceeding was initiated against him in which he was punished also, departmentally.
But when the matter was remanded to consider afresh by order dated 12.02.2015, the two authorities refused to grant the benefit of Regulation 241 of the Police Regulations on the ground that the charges are not one and same in both the proceedings i.e.
criminal and departmental and both the charges are different, whereas, as noticed above, though the departmental proceeding is based on Regulation 64(11) of the Police Regulations, but the basis of invoking Regulation 64(11) is criminal behaviour i.e. the offence punishable under Sections 306 &
498A of the IPC for which he was admittedly acquitted on 28.05.1997 honourably by the criminal court and criminal appeal preferred against his acquittal has been dismissed by this Court by affirming the judgment of acquittal.
Therefore, it is clearly established that Regulation 241 of the Police Regulations is squarely attracted, as he has been tried for offence under Sections 306 & 498A of the IPC and he has been acquitted by the criminal court and his acquittal has been affirmed by this Court in criminal appeal.
Thus, as a matter of right, by Regulation 241 he is entitled to be reinstated as he cannot be punished departmentally for the offence for which he has been tried and acquitted clearly.
